chunks: His people argued with him, and he said: 'Do you argue with me about God, while He has guided me? And I do not fear what you associate with Him, except that my Lord wills; for my Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then reflect?'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'He has guided me' in the context of arguing with idolaters?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is frequently cited to demonstrate the logical superiority of monotheism over idolatry, with many scholars identifying the speaker as Prophet Hud addressing the people of 'Aad, though some attribute it to Ibrahim. The phrase 'except what my Lord wills' (إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ رَبِّي شَيْئاً) is interpreted not as a concession to divine decree overriding free will, but as a reference to the specific instances of idol power granted by God, such as in the case of the elephant or the fire. This highlights the concept of 'suffah' (comprehensive knowledge) of Allah, inviting rational reflection ('afala tathakkarun') as a primary method for recognizing divine unity.
